# the contributor audit: all-dimensional lower frustum dual and preserving birth geometry

## All-dimensional lower dual

Source: `candidate c7808043ad51b327`.

Analytic audit PASS. The ratio Rratio=(s-1)/(2s-J) decreases on its positive-denominator interval because J is strictly concave and J(1)>2. The domain is indeed one terminal interval. The endpoint numerator has exactly the stated expansion N=Aq+constant+Bq^(-d)-Cq^(1-d)-Dq^(1-2d).

Differentiating twice gives the stated G. Its derivative has one affine sign change, and the concave endpoint bound for f(r)=(d+1)r-2r^d proves G(1)>=0; the binomial comparison applies to every integer d>=2. Thus N'' changes from nonnegative to nonpositive at most once on[1,infinity), and N' has no interior minimum on[R,infinity).

The lower endpoint derivative factor is exactly (1+t*-2p)[e*+t*/(2p)]+2s*t'(s*)(e*-1). Both summands are nonnegative, with the second using two negative factors. At infinity N' tends to A=1+e*-2v*>=0. Finally N(R)>=0 is exactly the independently proved beta(t*)<=1/2. This establishes all of the claimed lower inequality, with no mixture centering needed at that step. The upper dual remains a separate obligation.

## Birth response and preliminary path

Source: `candidate 8b9ef51c1503d49a`, as corrected after Topological's projection-entry audit.

The covariance numerator of epsilon^(1/d)D scales as epsilon^(1+2/d), so the pooled within-fiber covariance derivative is -Sigma/M. Hence the old-cap width correction is A/(2M), with A<=0. A fixed finite smoothed menu has a uniform O(epsilon^(1+1/d)) spatial error from the new fibers, and its first mass derivative is the limiting capture profile. The selected finite-envelope and complete-new-candidate hypotheses are still necessary; no global source assertion follows from the derivative alone.

The corrected preliminary Minkowski path is valid: it stays between the old and extended bodies, fixes every old fiber, and any new sampled trace is a subset of its prescribed singleton. New exposed sampled bases can appear before the last time because the real projection can overhang, but their mass and depth remain zero. The proof now uses exactly this, without asserting a false projection-entry time. The ordinary zero-width version correctly requires strict birth margins and separate threshold regularity.

## Geometric extension test and global cover

Source: `candidate f66dcff3eb3e1f03`.

The representation-polytope test is exact: at an old base, every possible new fiber point belongs to a Minkowski combination indexed by that polytope, and its support function is linear in the coefficients. Its finitely many vertices therefore suffice. For d>=1, a new intermediate lattice base in conv(P,q) receives a positive homothetic copy of a positive real fiber of the canonical old body. Thus the stated no-extra-lattice-point condition is necessary and sufficient for a point-only birth beyond P.

The global Doignon upgrade follows from the already globally lattice-free auxiliary Q, including its empty-original-intersection construction. The latter uses permitted perturbations of auxiliary normals, positive spanning for coercivity, an attained first common expansion point, and nonvertical cap-mass continuity. It does not impose genericity on C. It loses original-support integer facet witnesses, as explicitly stated.

The four-fiber example excludes EVERY new integer extension point by the forced interval length kb/(k+1)>=b/2>a. Its four caps nevertheless define an actual globally lattice-free diamond and cover every integer plane. The exact simultaneous endpoint contraction lowers its depth to1/4. Therefore global coverage alone does not imply a preserving birth; the obstruction is not a below-OC minimum.
